articles.title: Mapping Gadolinium-based Contrast Agent Residues in the Rat Kidney.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs) are routinely used to enhance magnetic resonance (MR) imaging. In recent years, GBCA residues were detected in multiple organs, with the kidney as the primary organ of excretion showing the highest concentrations. This study aimed to map the intricate spatial distribution of GBCA residues in rat kidneys at an early and a late time point. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Rats received one of 6 marketed GBCAs [3 macrocyclic, 3 linear; cumulative dose 4.8 mmol gadolinium (Gd)/kg] or saline and were sacrificed at day 5 or week 14 post administration (n = 5 per GBCA and time point). In whole renal tissue slices, the distribution of elemental Gd was determined by laser ablation-inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry and the distribution of intact GBCA chelates by matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization-mass spectrometry imaging. In ex vivo kidneys, MR relaxometry was used to assess MR-detectable GBCA residues. RESULTS: At day 5, Gd was predominantly localized in the renal cortex across all GBCAs, with 10- to 100-fold lower medullary levels. Distribution patterns corresponded well with those of exemplary intact GBCA chelates. At week 14, Gd levels had decreased by 1 to 2 orders of magnitude. Distribution patterns from linear GBCAs showed Gd remaining predominantly in the cortex, while Gd from macrocyclic GBCAs was similar in cortex and medulla. Several GBCAs exhibited a prominent Gd presence at the transition zone between outer and inner medulla. Intact chelate was only detectable for the exemplary macrocyclic GBCA, with a spatial distribution pattern matching that of elemental Gd. MR relaxometry detected GBCA residues within ex vivo kidneys but also in the surrounding water-based fixative. This indicated the presence and washout of intact GBCAs, which was greater for macrocyclic versus linear GBCAs. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first comprehensive spatially resolved characterization of renal GBCA residues at an early and a late time point. GBCA residues exhibited specific intrarenal distribution patterns and distinct changes in these patterns over the course of their elimination. Our findings of specific retention patterns suggest that renal microanatomy and local physicochemical conditions play critical roles in GBCA retention. These insights provide a foundation for future investigations into retention mechanisms and potential long-term tissue effects.

articles.title: C3E-RRG:Confounder-Aware Causal Evidence Coupling and Evolution for Chest X-Ray Report Generation.
articles.abstract: Chest X-ray report generation aims to produce diagnostic descriptions grounded in imaging evidence. However, correlation-driven models may exploit reporting templates and disease co-occurrence patterns, leading to unsupported findings and semantic drift. To address this issue, we propose C3E-RRG, a confounder-aware causal debiasing framework for chest X-ray report generation that incorporates explicit causal modeling into the encoder-decoder pipeline. Specifically, we first construct confounding variables by combining language priors derived from pointwise mutual information with disease co-occurrence statistics, and apply confounder-aware adjustment to suppress spurious correlations induced by data bias. We then design an evidence-consistent cross-modal coupling module to strengthen the correspondence between visual features and diagnostic semantics, thereby reducing semantic drift caused by high-frequency reporting templates. Finally, we develop a dynamic bidirectional causal evolution mechanism that iteratively revisits visual evidence and refines semantic representations, progressively correcting semantic deviations and improving image-text consistency during long-sequence generation. Experiments on the IU-XRay and MIMIC-CXR datasets demonstrate competitive performance and validate the effectiveness of the proposed components in suppressing confounding effects, aligning visual evidence with diagnostic semantics, and dynamically correcting generation errors. The source code is available at https://github.com/ cloneiq/C3E-RRG.

articles.title: Identification of local nonlinear shear-wave dynamics using Volterra kernels: application to prostate cancer detection.
articles.abstract: Cancer remains a major health concern worldwide. Shear-wave elastography (SWE) holds promise for cancer detection by quantifying linear elastic changes in tissue through shear-wave (SW) velocity estimation. However, shear viscosity and nonlinearity are often over-looked, despite their potential as additional biomarkers. This study evaluates the visco-hyperelastic properties of soft tissue, including linear shear modulus, shear viscosity, and shear nonlinearity. We propose using Volterra kernels to characterize local nonlinear SW dynamics, with kernel identification based on SW particle velocity measurements at adjacent locations. The method was validated using in-silico simulations and in-vitro gelatin phantoms. To evaluate its clinical relevance, we applied the method for prostate cancer (PCa) detection. To our knowledge, this is the first in-vivo assessment of voxel-based visco-hyperelastic properties of the prostate. In 90 patients, our results indicated that the linear kernel correlated with the linear shear modulus, while the quadratic kernel reflected both viscosity and nonlinearity. A convolutional neural network trained on these parameters with registered histopathology as ground truth achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.60 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.57, 0.62) and 0.66 (95% CI: 0.64, 0.68) for PCa detection, respectively-both significantly outperforming the linear shear modulus (AUC of 0.54; 95% CI, 0.52 to 0.56). Our findings suggest that Volterra kernels reflect information related to the visco-hyperelastic properties of prostate tissue, highlighting the potential of viscosity and nonlinearity as additional biomarkers for PCa detection.

articles.title: Evaluating strategies to optimize breast MRI screening: a modeling study of abbreviated protocols, dockable tables, and staffing scenarios.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: MRI is increasingly recommended for breast cancer screening, particularly in women with dense breast tissue. However, widespread adoption is constrained by limited capacity and high costs. This study evaluated how optimized MRI screening workflows could address these barriers through three targeted interventions: an abbreviated scan protocol, dockable MRI tables, and expanded technician staffing. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A calculation model was developed to compare seven workflow strategies against the current standard care. Strategies included reducing MRI acquisition time from 13 to 6 min, introducing dockable tables with breast coils, adding a third technician, and combinations thereof. Workflow durations and cost inputs were derived from published literature, hospital data, and expert opinion. Primary outcomes were daily screening capacity, cost per screening, annual screening costs, and staffing requirements for a screening volume of 5500 screening examinations per year. RESULTS: After evaluating several optimized workflow strategies, we found that reducing MRI acquisition time increased daily screening capacity from 30 to 47 scans, with associated annual savings of €147,505 (8.4%) and a reduction of 1320 technician hours. Combined strategies integrating reduced scan time, additional technicians, and dockable tables increased the daily capacity from 30 to 67 scans and reduced annual costs by up to €160,557 (9.2%) compared with the current workflow. CONCLUSIONS: Optimizing MRI breast cancer screening workflows with abbreviated scan protocols and dockable tables can substantially increase screening capacity, reduce costs, and technician workload. This would expand access to MRI screening, without requiring additional scanners, potentially providing a solution for (future) capacity problems. KEY POINTS: Question Which workflow optimization strategies, including abbreviated scan protocols, dockable tables, and additional technicians, offer the greatest capacity and cost benefits for MRI breast cancer screening? Findings Abbreviated scan protocols provide the largest cost savings, while combined workflow changes can substantially increase capacity and still reduce costs. Clinical relevance Optimizing MRI breast cancer screening workflows with abbreviated scans and dockable tables can increase screening capacity and reduce costs and technician workload. This expands access to MRI screening, without requiring additional scanners, potentially providing a solution for capacity problems.

Percutaneous and endovascular procedures in adrenal disease: indications, technique, and outcomes.
articles.abstract: Adrenal masses are found on roughly 4-5% of abdominal imaging studies, and the proportion rises with age. Most are benign, non-functioning adenomas that need imaging characterization and hormonal screening but no intervention. The remainder, comprising metastases, adrenocortical carcinoma, pheochromocytoma and hormonally active adenomas, raise questions that computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging cannot always settle; in these cases image-guided procedures can help. Percutaneous biopsy is reserved for hormonally inactive lesions whose benignity imaging has not established and whose histology would change management. Adrenal venous sampling remains the reference method for lateralizing aldosterone excess in primary aldosteronism and therefore decides who is offered adrenalectomy, although success depends heavily on operator experience and local protocol. Thermal ablation has produced biochemical and blood-pressure responses in selected aldosterone-producing adenomas and local control of limited metastases, but the evidence is largely nonrandomized and does not establish equivalence with surgery. Transarterial embolization serves three purposes: hemostasis in adrenal hemorrhage, devascularization before resection of hypervascular tumors, and functional treatment of aldosteronism, now supported by one small randomized trial. Each procedure carries hazards peculiar to the gland (catecholamine crisis, adrenal insufficiency after bilateral treatment, non-target embolization) that shape patient selection and periprocedural monitoring. This review covers indications, technique, outcomes and complications for each. Surgery remains the treatment of choice for most operable patients. Interventional radiology is most useful when the indications for sampling, ablation or embolization are recognized early and discussed at the multidisciplinary meeting, not only after surgery has been declined.

articles.title: Multiparametric quantitative MRI in knee osteoarthritis: evidence and requirements for interpretation and reporting.
articles.abstract: Quantitative MRI can characterize cartilage and other joint tissues beyond visible structural damage, but its contribution to individual management of knee osteoarthritis remains uncertain. This narrative review examines the evidence needed to interpret quantitative measurements, combine parameters, and report their uncertainty. An initial PubMed search in June 2026 was supplemented on 14 September 2026 by an updated PubMed search and broader Embase and Web of Science searches. Targeted full-text assessment addressed incremental value, outcome timing, validation, and measurement error. Selected development studies found better discrimination with integrated diffusion and relaxation measurements than with individual parameters, whereas other combined imaging models did not improve on simpler comparators. Longitudinal associations were outcome-specific, and independent external validation was limited. Treatment studies showed inconsistent agreement between imaging changes and symptomatic benefit. We propose a five-step interpretation framework that establishes the clinical question, verifies technical adequacy, assesses morphology and comparable reference data, evaluates measurement uncertainty, and separates observations from clinical inferences. Two hypothetical scenarios illustrate its application. Quantitative MRI currently provides its strongest support as a controlled research measurement. Demonstrated reproducibility, an appropriate comparator, and evidence of added decision value are required before a quantitative finding can justify patient-level diagnostic, prognostic, or treatment-response claims.

articles.title: Performance of Deep Learning Algorithms for Segmentation of Shoulder Anatomy on MRI: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: To synthesize the performance and methodological characteristics of fully automated deep learning algorithms for shoulder magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) segmentation. This systematic review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. CENTRAL, PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore were searched from inception through July 17, 2026. The protocol specified fully automated deep learning-based pixel-wise segmentation of shoulder MRI, an expert-derived MRI-space reference standard, and quantitative segmentation metrics. Two reviewers independently screened records; unresolved disagreements were adjudicated by a senior reviewer. Overlapping datasets were linked during synthesis. Of 354 identified records, 169 duplicates were removed, 185 records were screened, and 53 full-text reports were assessed. Thirty-five reports were included (31 journal articles and 4 full conference papers; 2018-2026). U-Net-based encoder-decoder architectures predominated, with additional region-based, transformer, adversarial, and autoencoder approaches. Dice similarity coefficients ranged from approximately 0.81-0.99 for osseous targets, 0.71-0.99 for shoulder muscles, and 0.58-0.94 for tendon or tear regions; intersection-over-union values for tear or surgical-planning regions ranged from 0.45-0.83. MRI protocols and validation designs were heterogeneous, and most reports described retrospective single-center investigations. Five reports used independent external test sets; several others included multicenter images. Overlapping cohorts precluded a valid pooled participant count. Deep learning achieved high accuracy for shoulder bones and rotator-cuff muscles in selected datasets, whereas tear-region performance was more variable. Multicenter patient-level validation and standardized annotation and reporting are needed before routine clinical deployment.

Circulating Tumor DNA and Cell-Free DNA as Candidate Biomarkers After Image-Guided Locoregional Therapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma and Colorectal Liver Metastases: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To review ctDNA and cfDNA as biomarkers after locoregional therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and colorectal liver metastases (CRLM). MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science were searched (July 2026) for ctDNA/cfDNA studies in HCC or CRLM patients undergoing TACE, Y90, or ablation; Newcastle-Ottawa Scale assessed risk of bias. RESULTS: Eleven studies were included (eight HCC, three CRLM; n≈820). Pre-treatment ctDNA mutations predicted survival after TACE (CTNNB1: HR 5.3, 95% CI 1.4-20.6; TP53: HR 5.3, 95% CI 1.4-10.1; KEAP1: HR 22.0, 95% CI 2.2-221.0). A cfDNA/ctDNA score stratified progression-free survival after TACE (1.3 vs 10.3 months; p=0.002). ctDNA predicted death after ablation in HCC (HR 2.6, 95% CI 1.5-4.7; p=0.001) and recurrence in CRLM (HR 2.97, 95% CI 1.47-6.03; P=0.003). Y90 evidence was limited. CONCLUSION: CtDNA and cfDNA correlated with treatment outcomes after locoregional therapy; evidence is heterogeneous and biomarker-driven trials are required before clinical implementation.

Free-breathing fast abdominal simultaneous T1, T2, PD and B1 mapping via deep learning reconstruction.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Multi-parametric quantitative MRI (mqMRI) enables non-invasive tissue characterization and holds significant clinical value in abdominal imaging. Conventional methods are restricted by long acquisition times and motion artifacts induced by physiological processes and irregular breathing, leading to registration errors between sequential acquisitions. PURPOSE: To develop and evaluate a framework for abdominal quantitative imaging under free-breathing conditions with reduced scan time and improved robustness to motion. METHODS: A novel framework integrating the longitudinal magnetization-controlled multiple overlapping-echo detachment (LMC-MOLED) sequence with synthetic data-driven deep learning reconstruction was proposed. To generate the synthetic dataset for training, a respiratory motion model combining global and local displacement vector fields was developed, ensuring temporal alignment with the inter-phase intervals of LMC-MOLED acquisitions. By applying interpolation to the original template, virtual imaging objects were generated to simulate respiratory-induced deformations while preserving anatomical textures, tissue boundaries, and inter-slice correlations. These objects were subsequently processed with MRI Bloch simulation to generate the final synthetic dataset, which was used to train a BGA-Multi-UNet architecture for motion correction and improved quantitative accuracy. RESULTS: The proposed framework enabled simultaneous mapping of T1, T2, proton density, and B1 under free-breathing conditions. With a 5-slice interleaved acquisition, the average acquisition time was reduced to approximately one second per slice without the need for respiratory gating. Both numerical and in vivo experiments demonstrated high accuracy and repeatability, with image quality comparable to conventional breath-hold acquisitions while mitigating motion-induced artifacts. CONCLUSION: This framework offers a rapid and reliable solution for multi-parametric abdominal imaging under free-breathing conditions. The combination of synthetic motion modeling with deep learning reconstruction enables accurate quantitative mapping with effective motion correction, offering potential clinical benefits for efficient and robust abdominal magnetic resonance imaging.

articles.title: Impact of correlated PBPK parameters on intra-patient global sensitivity analysis in molecular radiotherapy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models integrated into digital twins provide a robust framework for optimizing individualized molecular radiotherapy (MRT). Nevertheless, uncertainties in PBPK-model-derived dosimetry can compromise the reliability of dosimetry-guided treatment planning and individualized therapy decisions. PURPOSE: This study employs intra-patient global sensitivity analysis (GSA) to assess the influence of uncertainty and correlations among PBPK model parameters on estimated kidney and tumor absorbed doses (ADs) in prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted theragnostics. METHODS: Data from 10 patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who underwent pre-therapeutic [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-I&T PET/CT and a cycle of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-I&T therapy, followed by post-therapeutic SPECT/CT scans at Days 1 and 4 post-injection, were analyzed. A previously established whole-body PBPK model for PSMA-targeted radionuclide therapy was used as the baseline model. Fifteen model parameters, their standard errors, and inter-parameter correlations were estimated by fitting to measured time-activity data and subsequently evaluated using intra-patient GSA based on the Kucherenko method implemented in UQLab. In one approach, correlations were ignored to identify the direct influences of uncertainty in input parameters on ADs. In a second approach, correlations were included to reflect realistic parameter distributions and to capture indirect effects arising from parameter interdependencies. Pharmacokinetics were simulated to estimate therapeutic kidney and tumor ADs as well as main- and total-effect indices (  S i , S i T )   . Sensitivity indices, ADs, and their associated uncertainty metrics were compared between scenarios with and without parameter correlations. RESULTS: Including parameter correlations in the GSA yielded kidney ADs of 4.2 Gy [3.0-7.2 Gy] (median [min-max]) with standard deviations (SDs) of 0.5 Gy [0.4-0.9 Gy] and tumor ADs of 10.1 Gy [2.0-26.8 Gy] with SDs of 1.7 Gy [0.6-3.4 Gy]. Neglecting correlations resulted in significantly higher uncertainties in ADs, by a factor of 1.2 [1.0-1.8] for both kidneys and tumors. Kidney ADs were most sensitive to kidney receptor density (  S i = 0.3  [ 0.1 -  0.6 ] ,   S i T = 0.7  [ 0.6 - 0.8 ]   ) and to the filtered fraction of renal blood flow ( S i = 0.2  [ 0.1 - 0.3 ] ,   S i T = 0.3  [ 0.1 - 0.4 ] )   . Tumor ADs were most affected by tumor receptor density (  S i = 0.7  [ 0.1 - 1.0 ] ,   S i T = 0.8  [ 0.3 - 1.0 ]   ). The involvement of parameter correlations did not alter the identification of the parameters most influential on AD estimates and further reduced computational runtime. CONCLUSIONS: Incorporating parameter correlations into intra-patient GSA reduced the estimated uncertainty associated with ADs, underscoring the importance of preserving parameter dependencies when propagating uncertainty in PBPK-based individualized MRT. The identification of key PBPK parameters governing kidney and tumor ADs remained stable when including correlation, confirming the robustness of the underlying model structure.

articles.title: A multi-reader multi-case study comparing Breast Cancer Reading Efficiency and Accuracy in Screening with Tomosynthesis versus AI-assisted mammography.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Full-field digital mammography (FFDM) is the standard for breast cancer screening but has reduced sensitivity in dense breasts. Digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) improves cancer detection compared to 2D mammography but is limited by cost and longer reading times. Artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced mammography has demonstrated improved sensitivity compared to 2D mammography. This study compares AI-enhanced 2D mammography (DM+AI) with DBT in recalling interval breast cancers (IBCs). METHODS: : A multi-reader, multi-case crossover study was conducted using the Emory BrEast Imaging Dataset, which includes paired FFDM and DBT images with biopsy-proven outcomes. Six radiologists reviewed 53 IBC and 53 screen-detected cancer (SDC) cases, with random assignment to DM+AI or DBT, followed by crossover after a washout period. Primary outcomes included recall rate of IBCs. Secondary outcomes included recall rate of SDCs, interpretation time, and subgroup analysis by breast density. RESULTS: : For IBCs, DM+AI and DBT demonstrated similar recall rates (41.5% vs 40.9%) and detection rates (14.8% vs 11.9%). DM+AI identified more non-invasive (31.5% vs 13.0%) and mass-forming (61.0% vs 21.8%) cancers. For SDCs, recall and detection rates were comparable across modalities. In fatty breasts, recall was higher with DM+AI (91.7% vs 50.0%), while DBT performed better in extremely dense breasts. DM+AI enabled faster interpretation, averaging 24.1 seconds less per case. CONCLUSION: : AI-enhanced 2D mammography demonstrated comparable performance to DBT with shorter interpretation times, supporting a stratified screening approach. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This study is the first direct comparison of AI-enhanced mammography and digital breast tomosynthesis for IBC detection.

articles.title: Comparative Study of Dual-energy X‑ray Absorptiometry versus Multislice Computed Tomography for Vertebral Height Measurement.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study investigates the discrepancies between two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) imaging-based approaches for vertebral height assessment. METHODS: Lumbar spine CT scans and dual-energy X‑ray absorptiometry (DXA) studies within 6 months were reviewed. Vertebral fracture assessment was performed by converting CT-measured height ratios into Genant grades using three methods: conventional (A), consensus (B), and global search (C). Dataset 1 included 34 patients (191 vertebrae; 1,302 CT slices) with CT and DXA; Dataset 2 included 114 patients with CT only. RESULTS: No significant difference was observed between Method A and DXA-based grading (p = 0.33). In contrast, Methods B and C significantly differed from DXA (p < 0.001, both). Discrepancies were greatest for vertebrae graded as 1 by Method A (98 and 166 vertebrae reclassified by Methods B and C, respectively). Compared with Method A, Method B revealed greater height reductions in Grades 0, 1, and 2 vertebrae by 9.00, 9.13, and 13.75 percentage points, respectively. For Method C, these reductions were 10.71, 10.14, and 12.35 percentage points, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Compared with DXA, continuous sagittal CT images improved detection of greatest vertebral height loss, especially for Grade 1 reductions. When applying 2D criteria to CT scans, clinicians should be cautious of a tendency to overestimate vertebral height loss. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This first study demonstrates that the 3D method yields vertebral height reduction 10.84 percentage points greater than the 2D method. Therefore, overestimation of vertebral height reduction on CT should be considered when radiological classification criteria are applied.

articles.title: Reliability-weighted patch learning for synthetic CT reconstruction in head and neck adaptive radiotherapy: A proof-of-concept study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is essential for adaptive radiotherapy (ART) but is limited by poor image quality. Existing deep learning methods for synthetic CT (sCT) generation face a critical trade-off: diffusion models offer high fidelity but are impractically slow, while fast-inference networks often lack structural accuracy and optimization stability. PURPOSE: To develop HQ-PatchNet, a reliability-driven deep learning framework designed to improve CBCT-to-sCT image quality while maintaining rapid inference speed for online ART workflows. METHODS: HQ-PatchNet utilizes a vision transformer (ViT)-integrated CycleGAN architecture. It introduces a reliability-driven, SSIM-based selective patch weighting mechanism controlled by a temperature decay schedule. This dynamically suppresses artifact-dominated regions and focuses optimization on anatomically reliable structures. The model was evaluated on 304 paired head-and-neck (HN) scans against conventional networks and recent diffusion models using quantitative metrics (MAE, SSIM, NCC, PSNR), computational speed, and clinical dosimetric accuracy (3D gamma index, 2%/2 mm). RESULTS: HQ-PatchNet improved image quality, reducing Mean Absolute Error (MAE) from 44.81 ± 11.24 HU to 11.85 ± 4.31 HU and achieving an SSIM of 0.960 ± 0.055, comparable to state-of-the-art diffusion models. Inference required only 6.42 ± 1.71 s per volume, compared to > 15 min for diffusion approaches. The model reduced severe metal and truncation artifacts, and representative qualitative assessment suggested visually consistent sCT generation under interfractional anatomical variation. Dosimetric assessment of complex HN IMRT plans yielded a high average gamma passing rate of 99.32 ± 0.56%. CONCLUSIONS: HQ-PatchNet provides a computationally efficient and clinically promising approach for daily CBCT-guided online ART by improving CBCT-to-sCT image quality while maintaining rapid inference speed. Further contour-based, multi-institutional, and multi-site validation remains necessary to confirm its broader clinical utility.

articles.title: Evidence of White Matter R2* Homogenization After Formalin Fixation.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Disentangling intrinsic susceptibility-driven R2* characteristics in white matter (WM) from fixation-related effects using in vivo, postmortem (PM) in situ, and formalin-fixed PM ex situ MRI. METHODS: DTI and multi-echo gradient-echo MRI were acquired in vivo, PM in situ and PM ex situ. PM cases included neurologically healthy individuals and patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Voxel-wise R2* values were obtained using a mono-exponential fit and evaluated both as whole WM averages and according to WM fiber-to-field orientation. For the PM ex situ orientation-dependency analysis, PM ex situ R2* data were registered to the corresponding in situ DTI acquisition. Averaged as well as orientation-dependent R2* profiles were pooled across WM and compared across conditions. RESULTS: Whole WM averaged and orientation-dependent R2* values differed across in vivo, PM in situ, and PM ex situ conditions. No differences were observed between PM in situ healthy and PM in situ ALS cases. Compared with in vivo measurements, both PM conditions showed elevated whole WM averaged R2* values and reduced orientation dependency, with the strongest R2* anisotropy in vivo and nearly absent orientation dependency in the PM ex situ condition. CONCLUSION: While orientation-dependent R2* is reduced but preserved in unfixed PM in situ tissue, it is largely eliminated after prolonged formalin fixation without rehydration, likely due to microstructural reorganization and protein cross-linking. Collectively, these findings indicate that orientation-dependent R2* measured in fixed tissue has limited translational validity, while underscoring its sensitivity to intact microstructural organization in vivo and in unfixed PM tissue.

articles.title: Rep2Rep-Shuffle: Shuffled Repetition-to-Repetition Learning for Noise-Adaptive Self-Supervised MRI Denoising.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: MRI applications with low SNR, such as non-proton imaging and low-field imaging, often require multiple signal averages to achieve adequate image quality at the cost of longer scan times. This work proposes Rep2Rep-Shuffle, a self-supervised learning framework that improves MRI denoising performance in repeated-acquisition imaging with limited training datasets. METHODS: Rep2Rep-Shuffle extends our previously proposed repetition-to-repetition learning (Rep2Rep)-based self-supervised denoising approach with a new shuffled repetition pairing strategy. Instead of using a fixed split between training input and target repetitions, different repetition combinations are randomly generated during training epochs for each dataset, which increases the effective training space when training datasets are limited. In addition, the framework also extends from slice-wise 2D to 3D denoising by exploiting correlations across all spatial dimensions. The proposed method was tested in vivo using sodium MRI and further validated using synthetic noisy MRI datasets. Different training strategies for both 2D and 3D denoising were compared. RESULTS: In vivo sodium MRI results demonstrated improved denoising and better preservation of anatomical structures with 3D Rep2Rep-Shuffle compared with fixed pairing (Rep2Rep) and 2D denoising. Reader evaluation further confirmed that 3D Rep2Rep-Shuffle received higher scores for different assessment categories. In synthetic experiments, 3D Rep2Rep-Shuffle achieved the best performance among self-supervised methods and approached the performance of supervised learning. CONCLUSION: Rep2Rep-Shuffle outperforms Rep2Rep for MRI denoising by increasing training diversity through shuffled repetition pairing and by leveraging volumetric spatial correlations. The method is particularly suited for low-SNR MRI applications that acquire multiple repetitions but have limited training datasets.

articles.title: Accelerated MR Elastography Using Learned Neural Network Representation.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop a deep-learning method for achieving fast high-resolution MR elastography from highly undersampled data without the need for high-quality training datasets. METHODS: We first reframed the deep neural network representation as a nonlinear extension of the linear subspace model, then used it to represent and reconstruct MRE image repetitions from undersampled k-space data. A multi-level k-space consistency loss was proposed to learn the network weights and mitigate overfitting. To further enhance reconstruction quality, phase-contrast specific magnitude and phase priors were incorporated, namely the similarity of anatomical structures and smoothness of wave-induced harmonic displacement. The network was trained in a self-supervised manner with empirically fixed iterations. Experiments were conducted using one multi-slice spin-echo and two 3D gradient-echo spiral MRE datasets. RESULTS: Compared to conventional linear subspace-based approaches, the nonlinear network representation method produced superior image reconstruction with suppressed artifacts and noise from a single in-plane spiral arm per MRE repetition, yielding stiffness estimation (e.g., from a 3D GRE sequence at 2 mm resolution within 1 min, R = 10) comparable to that obtained from fully sampled data. CONCLUSION: This work demonstrated the feasibility of using deep network representations to model and reconstruct MRE images from highly undersampled data, a nonlinear extension of the subspace-based approach. Future work will include validation on a larger and more diverse cohort of subjects to further assess its robustness and generalizability.

articles.title: Recursive partitioning analysis model based on 18F-FDG PET/CT metabolic parameters for recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma treated with PD-1 inhibitors and chemotherapy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: We aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of baseline 18F-FDG PET/CT metabolic parameters and to construct a risk stratification model for recurrent/metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (rmNPC) patients receiving first-line PD-1 inhibitors plus chemotherapy. METHODS: A total of 148 rmNPC patients from two centers were included. Whole-body total lesion glycolysis (wTLG), whole-body metabolic tumor volume (wMTV), and maximal standardized uptake values (SUVmax) were assessed. Predictive performance was evaluated via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, while progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were identified using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses. A recursive partitioning analysis (RPA) model was subsequently developed and validated for risk stratification. RESULTS: Lower baseline wTLG and wMTV were associated with better response and longer PFS and OS, with wTLG showing the highest predictive power (AUC = 0.776). The RPA model stratified patients into low-risk (low wTLG), medium-risk (high wTLG without liver metastasis), and high-risk (high wTLG with liver metastasis) groups, demonstrating significantly different median PFS (30.7, 15.9, 7.1 months) and OS (43.7, 29.9, 14.7 months; all p < 0.001), and achieving an AUC of 0.839 for predicting 3-year disease progression. Radiotherapy improved survival outcomes in the low-risk group but not in the high-risk group. Analysis of 213 individual lesions revealed heterogeneous responses, with lymph node metastases showing the best response and liver metastases the poorest. CONCLUSION: Baseline PET/CT metabolic parameters, particularly wTLG, serve as powerful predictors of survival in NPC patients receiving chemoimmunotherapy. The wTLG-based RPA model provides a robust tool for risk stratification and holds promise for guiding individualized clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Skull-Base Synthetic CT from Brain MRI: Development, Independent-Center Validation, and Radiologist Evaluation.
articles.abstract: We developed and evaluated a deep learning pipeline for skull-base synthetic computed tomography (sCT) generation from routine non-contrast T1-weighted and T2-weighted brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), focusing on clinically relevant bony anatomy for neurosurgical and radiotherapy workflows. We retrospectively collected 184 manually registered T1/T2/CT triplets for training and internal validation (166/18 split) and 43 cases from a second center for independent-center validation. A three-dimensional Swin-UNETR generator was trained with bone-weighted multiscale reconstruction, perceptual, and adversarial losses. Two board-certified radiologists independently scored 16 skull-base structures, artifacts, and diagnostic acceptability on raw sCT in Hounsfield units (HU), without histogram matching; this blinded review was the primary endpoint. Acceptability was 76.7% for Rater 1 and 67.4% for Rater 2 (pooled 72.1%, cluster-robust 95% CI 58.5-82.6%), with mean structure scores from 2.67 to 4.85 out of 5. Raw sCT showed limited absolute HU calibration (global MAE 364 ± 50   HU, bone Dice 0.38 ± 0.09  ), with a compressed dynamic range in which air and soft tissue were overestimated and dense bone underestimated; histogram-matched outputs, reported as a secondary analysis, reached bone Dice 0.88 ± 0.03  and bone MAE 26.31 ± 5.03   HU. Halo artifacts were near-universal, and false-canal artifacts occurred in 21-30% of cases. The method shows promise as a radiation-free adjunct for skull-base visualization, but the present results do not support replacing dedicated CT for diagnostic, dosimetric, or physics-based applications.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance and Calibration of AI Models for Thyroid Ultrasound Malignancy Classification: From TN5000 to ThyroidXL.
articles.abstract: We evaluated cross-dataset transportability of three frozen encoders for binary benign-versus-malignant thyroid ultrasound classification using expert-defined nodule regions and one external cohort. Logistic regression classifiers using DINOv2, TinyUSFM, and ResNet18 features were developed on 3500 TN5000 images, calibrated on 477 duplicate-clean validation images and tested on 958 images. External evaluation used maximum image scores from 2083 ThyroidXL images in 739 patients with cytological or histopathological outcomes. No external retraining, recalibration or threshold adjustment was performed. Additional analyses evaluated four classifiers, encoder-recommended preprocessing and calibration intercepts and slopes. Internal areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) were 0.9081 for TinyUSFM, 0.8946 for DINOv2, and 0.8896 for ResNet18. Primary external AUROCs were 0.8464 (95% confidence interval, 0.8164-0.8731), 0.7954, and 0.7833, respectively. Sensitivities at frozen high-sensitivity thresholds were 0.9972, 0.9717, and 0.9887, but specificities were 0.1736, 0.1891, and 0.1373. External calibration intercepts were negative; slopes were 0.891, 0.645, and 0.697. DINOv2 ranked first externally with four of five classifiers. With recommended preprocessing, ResNet18 ranked first numerically (0.8329 versus 0.8214 for DINOv2); their paired difference was inconclusive. Encoder rankings depended on the classifier and preprocessing. These results apply to the three evaluated implementations, not pretraining strategies generally. Transported patient scores overestimated malignancy and had low specificity. Prospective assessment is needed before clinical use.

articles.title: Vision Transformer-Based Automated Ordinal Grading of Supraspinatus Tendon Pathology and a Quantitative Faithfulness Audit of Attribution Maps in Shoulder MRI.
articles.abstract: Rotator cuff disorders, most often of the supraspinatus tendon, are a leading cause of shoulder pain, and magnetic resonance imaging is the reference modality. Grading their progression is subject to inter-reader variability, and automated systems for the task are expected to justify themselves through attribution maps. This study asks whether they do. Four Vision Transformer tiers spanning a 54-fold parameter range were trained under one searched configuration and averaged into an unweighted ensemble. On 694 regionally annotated sections from 276 shoulders in 264 patients, the ensemble reached 0.9130 accuracy (95% CI, 0.8406-0.9710) and a 0.9431 quadratic weighted kappa on a 69-section, patient-level held-out test subset. The four tiers differed by at most 0.0580, inside the 0.07 resolution limit, so any capacity effect is bounded below it rather than shown absent. Seven attribution methods from four mechanism families were scored against an occlusion reference. Occlusion placed 16.82 times chance mass on the annotated region, the attribution methods 1.15 to 13.90. Against a random ordering of the same cells, occlusion separated the deletion and insertion curves by 0.4773, a margin no method reached, and two methods beat this baseline on deletion but lost on insertion. The method closest to the reference kept a correlation of 0.977 with its own map after half the network was randomized. Repeating the audit under a Gaussian blur fill left the ranking of all eight arms unchanged. An attribution map offered as clinical evidence therefore requires interventional validation, with its perturbation and grid sensitivity reported.

articles.title: Contrast-Free ADC Intensity Features for Early Neurological Deterioration in Lacunar Infarction: An Exploratory Comparison with Perfusion Imaging and Deep Learning.
articles.abstract: Early neurological deterioration (END) affects approximately one in five patients with acute lacunar infarction and is associated with poor functional outcome. Hypoperfusion on contrast-enhanced perfusion MRI has been linked to END, but perfusion imaging requires intravenous contrast and is not part of the routine acute workup for minor stroke. We explored whether intensity features of non-contrast structural MRI carry information on END, using the visually classified pattern from a contrast-enhanced perfusion study in the same patients as a reference. We analyzed a prospectively collected single-center cohort of patients with acute lacunar infarction who underwent MRI within 24 h of symptom onset, including diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) mapping, fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR), and dynamic susceptibility contrast perfusion imaging. END was defined as an increase of ≥ 2 points on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale within 72 h. One hundred patients with complete imaging and outcome data were included, of whom 20 (20.0%) developed END. Candidate predictors comprised intensity features of the infarct core and an 8-mm perilesional rim normalized to whole-brain intensity, 201 DWI texture features, and 22 clinical and laboratory variables. Models were evaluated by 10-times-repeated 5-fold stratified cross-validation with the decision threshold fixed at 0.5; feature selection and standardization were performed within training folds only. The visually classified perfusion pattern served as a contrast-based clinical benchmark. ADC intensity features discriminated END with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.699 (approximate patient-level 95% CI 0.56-0.84) and an area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.473 against a base rate of 0.200; at the fixed threshold, sensitivity was 52.0% and positive predictive value 27.9%. The perfusion pattern alone yielded a sensitivity of 70.0%, a specificity of 60.0% and a negative predictive value of 88.9% (balanced accuracy 0.650). The difference between the two predictors was small relative to the sampling uncertainty at 20 events, so neither superiority nor equivalence could be established. The strongest individual feature was the 75th percentile of normalized ADC within the infarct core (univariate AUC 0.702), with higher values in patients who deteriorated (median 0.615 versus 0.555, P = 0.005). Adding the perfusion pattern to the ADC features did not improve discrimination (AUC 0.665, 95% CI 0.645-0.684). The signal was confined to the ADC map: models built on DWI or FLAIR intensity alone performed below chance (AUC 0.463 and 0.453). More complex models did not reach the ADC model at this sample size: 201 DWI texture features reached an AUC of 0.566, clinical and laboratory variables at best 0.625, and an end-to-end 2.5D ResNet-18 0.404 with random initialization, 0.482 with ImageNet pretraining and 0.611 for a small network sized for the data. In this exploratory single-center study, ADC intensity features obtained without contrast were associated with END in acute lacunar infarction, with discrimination similar in magnitude to the contrast-enhanced perfusion benchmark; the cohort was too small to establish equivalence, and threshold-level performance is insufficient to guide monitoring. Texture analysis and deep learning could not be adequately trained with 20 events, so their relative merit cannot be judged. ADC appears to be the informative non-contrast sequence; the findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger, multicenter cohorts.

articles.title: DINOv3-SAM: Fusing Semantic and Anatomical Foundation Models for Robust Medical Image Classification.
articles.abstract: Robust medical image classification remains a persistent challenge due to heterogeneous acquisition protocols, label noise, and subtle inter-class variability. In chest radiography, these difficulties are compounded by shortcut learning from non-anatomical artifacts and projection variability, which severely undermine generalization. To address these limitations, we propose DINOv3-SAM, a dual-encoder framework that synergistically integrates complementary visual representations. The architecture combines a self-supervised DINOv3 vision transformer, which captures global semantic context, with the Segment Anything Model (SAM) image encoder, which provides anatomy-aware spatial features. The two feature streams are spatially aligned and adaptively refined through a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), which emphasizes informative channels and diagnostically relevant regions prior to classification. Notably, only the final DINOv3 layers are fine-tuned while SAM remains frozen, yielding a computationally efficient framework with only 5.3 million trainable parameters. We evaluate DINOv3-SAM across five public datasets spanning diverse modalities and diagnostic tasks: pediatric pneumonia classification, cardiomegaly detection, large-scale RSNA pneumonia detection, COVID-19 radiography, and dermatological lesion classification. A unified stratified train/validation/test protocol ensures consistent and fair evaluation across both binary and multi-class settings. Each configuration was trained three times with different random seeds, and comprehensive comparisons against reproduced CNN baselines and published state-of-the-art methods, supported by statistical significance testing, demonstrate improvements across most datasets and metrics. The proposed framework achieves a mean accuracy of 94.94% (±3.06) on pediatric pneumonia, 97.24% (±0.77) accuracy (AUC 0.998 ±0.001) on COVID-19 radiography, and a mean AUC of 0.8705 (±0.0445) on the challenging RSNA benchmark. These results underscore the efficacy of fusing self-supervised semantic representations with segmentation-informed anatomical cues to enhance robustness against dataset bias, acquisition variability, and cross-domain shifts. The proposed approach offers a reliable foundation for multi-dataset and multi-modality medical image classification in research-oriented decision-support systems.

articles.title: Integration of weight-bearing computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging for advanced musculoskeletal statistical shape modeling of the foot and ankle.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Statistical shape models (SSMs) from three-dimensional (3D) medical imaging describe morphology variation in normal and pathologic anatomy. Within the foot and ankle, weight-bearing computed tomography (WBCT) is used to characterize skeletal deformity but poorly visualizes soft tissue. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides improved evaluation of soft tissue structures but less accurate bone visualization. This methodologic analysis describes and tests reliability of a novel process to generate SSMs from coregistered MRI and WBCT structures. This method is illustrated via two example models: a combined musculoskeletal model and a distal tibia growth plate model. METHODS: Bilateral WBCTs and T1-weighted DIXON MRIs of the lower legs were collected from 14 individuals aged 8 to 18 with no prior lower limb surgery in a control group and hereditary neuropathy group. Bones were segmented from WBCT and manually aligned in MRI space. Alignment reliability was evaluated with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Six muscles were segmented semi-automatically and the distal tibia growth plate was manually segmented from MRI. Following cropping, size normalization, and alignment multi-domain SSMs were generated. SSMs were evaluated qualitatively through comparison with expected anatomy and quantitively by calculation of compactness, generalization, and specificity. RESULTS: The alignment method demonstrated excellent reliability with an intrarater ICC of 1 and interrater ICC of 0.999. The musculoskeletal model demonstrated expected atrophy in neuromuscular disease and the preliminary growth plate model showed variation in metaphyseal thickness. Both models demonstrated compactness, specificity, and generalization comparable to published SSMs, requiring 11 and 12 modes to account for 95% of population variance. CONCLUSION: This method allows for application of shape modeling to novel questions in musculoskeletal morphology through simultaneous modeling of bone and soft tissue anatomy. Limitations include manual registration and MRI resolution. This analysis presented examples of muscle and growth plate models, but has broader applications in musculoskeletal analysis.
articles.journal: Int J Comput Assist Radiol Surg

articles.title: Dedicated Versus Generic ePTFE-covered Stent-grafts for Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt in Decompensated Cirrhosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Overt Hepatic Encephalopathy and Shunt Dysfunction.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To estimate the pooled sub-distribution hazard ratio (sHR) of overt hepatic encephalopathy (OHE) and shunt dysfunction in patients with decompensated cirrhosis undergoing transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) using dedicated stent‑grafts (DSG) versus generic stent‑grafts (GSG), and to compare their estimated 1-year event risk, relative risk (RR), and risk difference (RD). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, major biomedical databases were searched for retrospective studies including adults with decompensated cirrhosis undergoing TIPS with DSG or GSG. Pooled estimates for sHR, one‑year cumulative incidence, RR, and RD for OHE and shunt dysfunction were calculated. RESULTS: The pooled estimated 1-year event risk of OHE was 14.3% (95% CI: 7.2-26.4%; I2 = 85%) with DSG and 17.4% (95% CI: 8.1-33.4%; I2 = 91%) with GSG, with no significant subgroup difference (p = 0.611). The RR for OHE with DSG versus GSG was 0.81 (95% CI: 0.51-1.28; p = 0.37; I2=55%), the RD was - 0.03 (95% CI: -0.13 to 0.06; p = 0.45; I2 = 82%), and the pooled sHR was 0.69 (95% CI: 0.13-3.66; p = 0.44; I2 = 78%), none reaching statistical significance. The estimated 1-year event risk of shunt dysfunction was 5.2% (95% CI: 2.6-10.2%; I2 = 63%) with DSG and 10.7% (95% CI: 7.8-14.7%; I2 = 39%) with GSG, with no significant subgroup difference (p = 0.080). DSG was associated with lower shunt dysfunction risk, with RR 0.41 (95% CI: 0.26-0.66; p = 0.0002; I2 = 0%), RD - 0.06 (95% CI: - 0.09 to - 0.03; p < 0.0001; I2 = 0%), and sHR 0.32 (95% CI: 0.17-0.59; p < 0.02; I2 = 0%). CONCLUSION: DSG use in TIPS was associated with significantly lower shunt dysfunction risk compared with GSG, while OHE risk does not differ between stent types. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Grade 3.

articles.title: Association of Capsular Involvement with Delayed Re-intervention After Splenic Artery Embolization for Blunt Splenic Injury.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate whether splenic capsule involvement is associated with delayed re-intervention after splenic artery embolization for blunt splenic injury. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 329 consecutive patients undergoing splenic artery embolization for blunt splenic injury (2017-2025). Capsule involvement was defined as a laceration reaching the splenic surface with capsular disruption or communication with the perisplenic space on contrast-enhanced computed tomography. The primary outcome was delayed re-intervention. Cox and Firth regression were performed, with interobserver agreement assessed by Cohen's kappa. RESULTS: Delayed re-intervention occurred in 26 patients (7.9%) at a median of 6 days; all underwent repeat embolization; none required splenectomy. Twenty (76.9%) were detected on routine surveillance computed tomography without preceding deterioration. Capsule involvement was present in 25 of 26 events. Initial computed tomography showed vascular injury elsewhere in 25 of 26 patients, but neither computed tomography nor angiography showed pseudoaneurysm or active bleeding at the eventual lesion site. Re-intervention occurred in 25 of 245 patients with capsule involvement (10.2%) versus 1 of 84 without (1.2%). Capsule involvement was associated with re-intervention (hazard ratio, 6.82; 95% confidence interval, 1.62-28.74; p = 0.009), but significance was lost after reclassifying two events. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were 96.2%, 27.4%, 10.2%, and 98.8%; pre-consensus agreement was 97.6% (Cohen's kappa = 0.938). CONCLUSION: Capsule involvement was associated with delayed re-intervention, but the estimate was statistically fragile because only one capsule-negative event occurred. Surveillance-driven, single-center findings are exploratory; external validation is required before changes in surveillance practice. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 3, prognostic study.

articles.title: Feasibility and Efficacy of Cryoablation as an Eyeball Salvage Therapy for Radiation-resistant Orbital/Choroidal Metastases.
articles.abstract: Orbital and choroidal metastases are rare and usually occur in disseminated disease. Treatment is palliative and aims to preserve visual function and maximize quality of life. When lesions progress despite radiotherapy, enucleation may become necessary, with major functional and psychological consequences. Cryoablation has been used in intraocular tumors such as retinoblastoma, but its use for orbital and choroidal metastases is rarely reported. We describe two patients in whom cryoablation was used as a minimally invasive, eye-preserving alternative to enucleation.

articles.title: Uterine Artery Embolization for Postpartum Hemorrhage: A 5-Year Single-Center Experience with Emphasis on Embolization Technique and Factors Associated with Clinical Failure.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe the embolization technique and clinical outcomes of uterine artery embolization (UAE) for refractory postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), and to identify variables associated with clinical failure. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 150 consecutive patients who underwent UAE for PPH at a single tertiary center (2021-2025). Clinical failure was defined as hysterectomy or repeat embolization (≥ 2 sessions). Variables associated with clinical failure were identified by univariable logistic regression and Fisher's exact test; pre-UAE transfusion was analyzed separately to assess reverse causality. RESULTS: Clinical success was achieved in 140/150 patients (93.3%); clinical failure occurred in 10/150 (6.7%), comprising hysterectomy in 4/10 and repeat embolization in 6/10. Uterine atony was the most common etiology (107/150, 71.3%). Additional vessel embolization was required in 47/150 patients (31.3%). In an exploratory subgroup analysis, emergency cesarean section had a higher failure rate than elective cesarean Sect. (5/32, 15.6% vs. 1/56, 1.8%; p = 0.022). On univariable analysis, higher total pRBC transfusion (OR 1.144; p = 0.003) and lower platelet count (OR 0.982; p = 0.023) were associated with clinical failure; pre-UAE transfusion was not (OR 1.168; p = 0.161), suggesting total pRBC reflects hemorrhage burden rather than antecedent risk. CONCLUSION: UAE achieved clinical success in 140/150 patients (93.3%); additional vessel embolization was required in 47/150 (31.3%). Total pRBC transfusion and platelet count were associated with clinical failure in univariable analysis; procedural variables were not. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4, Case Series.

articles.title: Automatic Ultrasound Habitat Radiomics for Differentiating Henoch-Schonlein Purpura Nephritis from IgA Nephropathy in Children: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To assess a noninvasive ultrasound habitat radiomics approach with automatic kidney segmentation for distinguishing pediatric Henoch-Schonlein purpura nephritis (HSPN) from immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included 592 biopsy-confirmed pediatric patients from three centers (HSPN, n = 338; IgAN, n = 254). The development cohort (n = 453) was split into training (n = 362) and internal validation (n = 91) cohorts, and an independent external validation cohort (n = 139) was used for final testing. Kidney regions of interest were automatically segmented using nnU-Net. K-means clustering defined three echogenic habitat subregions, and 408 radiomics features were extracted from the whole-kidney region and habitat subregions. Feature selection was performed in the training cohort, and three machine-learning classifiers were evaluated. The selected radiomics model was compared with clinical and combined models. RESULTS: nnU-Net achieved high kidney segmentation performance, with a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 0.957 and a mean intersection over union of 0.918 in the independent healthy-child test set. Fifteen radiomics features were retained, including six whole-kidney features and nine habitat-derived features. Logistic regression showed stable performance, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.806 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.715-0.897) internally and 0.825 (95% CI, 0.758-0.892) externally. The combined model outperformed the clinical model in AUC in both cohorts (0.846 vs 0.717; 0.805 vs 0.733). CONCLUSION: This deep-learning-assisted ultrasound habitat radiomics approach enabled automatic kidney delineation and showed encouraging performance as a reproducible imaging adjunct for differentiating pediatric HSPN from IgAN.

articles.title: Atrophy-Robust Multiclass CNN Segmentation of Brainstem-Related Structures in Neurodegenerative Parkinson Syndromes.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Neurodegenerative Parkinson syndromes show regionally distinct tissue loss involving several brainstem and midbrain structures. Reliable volumetry is constrained by atlas-based segmentation in atrophy-affected brains. We developed a multiclass convolutional neural network (CNN) for the segmentation of 16 brainstem-related regions on routine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 200 manually annotated MRI datasets of patients with Parkinson's disease, atypical Parkinson syndromes, and healthy controls were used for model development and validation. A Deep Neural Patchwork model was trained on 150 datasets and evaluated in an independent test cohort of 50 participants against atlas-based segmentation using the Dice coefficient, 95% Hausdorff distance, and average symmetric surface distances (ASSD). In an extended validation cohort of 264 participants, CNN-derived regional volumes were analyzed across Parkinson's disease, progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), and multiple system atrophy (MSA). RESULTS: CNN segmentation outperformed atlas-based segmentation across accuracy metrics. Overall medians were 0.75 vs 0.33 for Dice, 2.0 vs 5.0 mm for 95% Hausdorff distance, and 0.30 vs 1.02 mm for ASSD. CNN-derived volumetry recapitulated established disease-associated patterns, including predominant mesencephalic, superior cerebellar peduncle, and red nucleus atrophy in PSP and more marked pontine and middle cerebellar peduncle volume loss in MSA. CONCLUSION: The principal contribution of this study is an atrophy-robust multiclass brainstem segmentation framework. This framework may enable anatomically more faithful extraction of quantitative MRI metrics than atlas-based approaches and may reduce contamination from adjacent CSF spaces, particularly in small atrophy-affected structures.

articles.title: Isolated CSF Facet Effusions as a Predictor of Lateral Dural Tear Location in Spontaneous Intracranial Hypotension: A Multi-Institutional Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Ventral and lateral spinal dural tears are common causes of spontaneous intracranial hypotension, each requiring different myelographic approaches for leak localization. Spine MRI can infer the presence of a dural tear but has limited utility in localizing leaks. One recent case series described several patients with isolated facet effusions at the site of lateral dural tears. We investigated whether the presence of an isolated facet joint effusion on spine MRI could predict the type and location of a dural tear in patients with spontaneous intracranial hypotension. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We identified consecutive patients with precisely localized ventral or lateral dural tears on advanced myelography at three centers. A single neuroradiologist at each center assessed for isolated facet effusions on pre-myelographic spine MRIs, defined as fluid accumulation in a single facet joint that was visually greater than any other joint in the spine. Myelographic studies were reviewed to confirm leak type/location. The frequency of isolated facet effusions was compared between patients with lateral and ventral dural tears using Fisher's exact test. The proximity of facet effusions to leak level/side was assessed. RESULTS: Sixty-four patients (32 ventral and 32 lateral dural tears) were included. All patients had epidural CSF on MRI. Isolated facet effusions were more common in patients with lateral dural tears (21/32, 66%) compared with ventral dural tears (0/32, 0%) (p < .001). The effusion was at the same level and side as the leak in 11/21 (52%) patients and within one ipsilateral spinal level of the leak in 7/21 (33%) patients. Contrast filling of a facet joint was seen in 9/21 (43%) cases and corresponded to the site of MRI effusion in 8/9 (89%). CONCLUSIONS: Isolated facet joint effusions on spine MRI were seen exclusively in patients with lateral dural tears and were usually located at or within one ipsilateral spinal level of the leak. This finding may provide a useful imaging clue that there is an underlying lateral dural tear, which is helpful to plan optimal myelographic positioning and technique.

articles.title: Evaluation of Temporal Bone Image Quality with Low-Dose Photon-Counting CT in Cadaveric Heads.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) is an emerging technology that offers improved spatial resolution and noise reduction at lower radiation doses than conventional CT; however, the effect of dose reduction on clinically significant image quality has not been well established. Following the ALARA (As Low As Reasonably Achievable) principle, this study evaluated temporal bone image quality across decreasing radiation doses to identify the minimum dose required to maintain diagnostic integrity. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Seven cadaveric heads underwent temporal bone PCCT imaging at four tube current-time products: 290, 75, 25, and 11 mAs. All scans were acquired at 120 kV, 0.55 pitch, and a 0.5 second rotation time and reconstructed with 0.2-mm slice thickness in axial and coronal planes for left and right temporal bones. Three board-certified radiologists independently assessed prespecified, randomized temporal bone landmarks using a 5-point Likert scale to determine clinical utility (1-nondiagnostic; 5-excellent). Mixed-effects linear regression with random intercepts for patient, reader, and landmark estimated mean scores by dose. Pairwise comparisons were Tukey-adjusted, and one-sided FDR-adjusted t-tests evaluated whether predicted mean scores exceeded 3 (clinically sufficient). RESULTS: At 290 and 75 mAs, predicted mean scores were 4.81 (95% CI: 4.42-5.21) and 4.21 (95% CI: 3.82-4.61), respectively, demonstrating good/excellent image quality for all evaluated landmarks and exceeding threshold for clinical sufficiency (FDR-adjusted p<0.0001). At 25 mAs, predicted mean scores were 2.80 (95% CI: 2.41-3.19), falling in the poor/sufficient range, and at 11 mAs, were rated the lowest at 2.09 (95% CI: 1.70-2.48), scoring below the clinical sufficiency threshold (p=0.99). Overall, mean Likert image quality scores decreased with progressive mAs reduction, remaining technically interpretable but below the threshold for clinical sufficiency at 25 mAs. All pairwise comparisons were statistically significant (Tukey-adjusted p<0.0001). Interreader agreement (Krippendorff's α) ranged from 0.301 to 0.657 across landmarks. CONCLUSION: PCCT maintains clinically sufficient temporal bone image quality at tube current-time products as low as 75 mAs, while doses of 25 mAs and below fall below the threshold for reliable clinical use. Per ALARA, this threshold optimizes safety via significant dose reduction while maintaining the high image quality necessary for complex temporal bone anatomy.

articles.title: State-Dependent EEG Markers of Excitation/Inhibition and Hemodynamic State Are Associated with Random Noise Stimulation Effects.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-invasive brain stimulation effects vary substantially across individuals, yet the physiological factors associated with this variability remain unclear. OBJECTIVE: We tested whether baseline and task-related EEG markers of excitation/inhibition (E/I) and hemodynamic state are associated with the effects of transcranial random noise stimulation (tRNS) on learning. METHODS: Participants completed a mathematical learning task during active or sham tRNS. We indexed E/I-related population dynamics using the EEG aperiodic exponent, for which lower values have been linked to relatively greater excitation than inhibition, and assessed hemodynamic state using fNIRS-derived oxygenated hemoglobin (HbO). Behavioral learning was modeled using generalized linear mixed-effects models. RESULTS: tRNS accelerated learning relative to sham stimulation but did not reliably induce pre-post changes in resting-state aperiodic exponent or HbO. Instead, stimulation effects were state-dependent. Higher resting-state aperiodic exponent and lower resting-state HbO were associated with greater behavioral gains under tRNS, while task-related aperiodic exponent was associated with stimulation-related differences in learning. Task-evoked HbO was associated with learning rate but did not significantly differentiate stimulation effects. Across modalities, the findings identify complementary electrophysiological and hemodynamic correlates of variability in learning under stimulation. However, statistical support for the EEG moderation effects was attenuated in models including participant-specific learning slopes, indicating sensitivity to random-effects specification and the need for replication. CONCLUSIONS: The findings argue against a simple tonic-shift account of tRNS and support a state-dependent framework in which stimulation effects depend on ongoing electrophysiological and hemodynamic context. EEG and fNIRS provided complementary information about variability in learning and stimulation response, supporting multimodal approaches to understanding and individualizing neuromodulation.

articles.title: Do autistic traits modulate the neural processing of logical rule violations in visual and auditory modalities?
articles.abstract: Similarities in cognitive processing have been reported between individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and non-clinical individuals with autistic traits. However, previous research on autistic traits has primarily focused on social-emotional domains, with limited attention to abstract logical reasoning. Given that sensitivity to rules and patterns is a notable characteristic of the autism spectrum, logical rule processing may be particularly informative for understanding cognitive differences associated with autistic traits. The present research aimed to investigate the behavioral and neural responses of students with autistic traits to logical and illogical number sequences through two event-related potential studies. Based on Autism Spectrum Quotient-10 (AQ-10) scores, participants were categorized into High-AQ and Low-AQ groups. In Study 1, both groups judged whether visually presented logical and illogical three number sequences followed a logical incremental rule. In Study 2, both groups performed the same task as in Study 1, except number sequences were presented in the auditory modality. No significant group difference was found in response to logical number sequences in either study. However, relative to the Low-AQ group, the High-AQ group exhibited larger P2 and P3 amplitudes and more negative emotional reactions to illogical number sequences in the visual modality (Study 1), and more positive N1 and LPP amplitudes, and higher arousal ratings to illogical number sequences in the auditory modality (Study 2). These findings suggest that students with autistic traits may exhibit altered neural responses and heightened emotional reactivity specifically to stimuli that violate logical rules in separate visual and auditory studies.

articles.title: Same Networks, Different Dynamics: Parsimony in Auditory Cognitive Task Processing.
articles.abstract: Distinct cognitive states might be supported either by dedicated, task-specific brain networks or by flexible modulation within shared ones, a distinction central to understanding how the brain allocates neural resources. Guided by the principle of parsimony, we hypothesized that both language and numerical cognition, when matched for sensory modality and attentional demand, would engage a common network architecture differentiated primarily through targeted modulation of connectivity strength and temporal dynamics rather than wholesale reconfiguration. We applied a jackknife-based dynamic functional connectivity approach to examine time-varying network engagement during auditory language comprehension and auditory math problem-solving in 172 age- and sex-matched participants from the Human Connectome Project-Young Adult cohort, using the Desikan-Killiany atlas and an 85% participation threshold. Of the significant connections identified, many were retained across both tasks, with 87 connections common to story and math, compared with 26 story-associated and 11 math-associated connections. Rather than indicating a novel shared-core architecture, this overlap is consistent with prior evidence that task functional connectivity is strongly constrained by a common intrinsic connectivity backbone. We therefore used the shared edge set as a common network framework for testing how two modality-matched, but cognitively distinct auditory tasks differ in connectivity strength and temporal variability. Among the 87 shared connections, 84 showed significant task-related differences in mean connectivity strength, indicating that story-math differentiation was expressed primarily through quantitative modulation of shared connections rather than wholesale changes in edge membership. Exploratory rolling-correlation analyses further suggested that some edges may show temporal variability in math-story connectivity correspondence even when mean connectivity strength is similar, highlighting a potential dynamic feature not captured by static connectivity estimates alone. Together, these findings suggest that story and math processing rely on a broadly shared connectivity backbone, while task differentiation emerges through graded modulation of connection strength and, in some cases, temporal variability.

articles.title: A systematic evaluation of lattice radiation therapy: from automated vertex placement to dosimetric criteria.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aims to establish a predictive, standardized lattice radiotherapy (LRT) workflow by systematically evaluating crystallographic close-packing strategies, formulating volume-stratified parameter guidelines, and implementing an integrated dosimetric evaluation framework. APPROACH: Lattice structures (4,095 configurations) were constructed across 21 patients with bulky tumours (613-1909 cm³) utilising three automated close-packing models (face-centred cubic [FCC], axial hexagonal close-packed [HCPxoy], and coronal rotated [HCPyoz]) parameterised by vertex diameter (Dlat) and the ratio of centre-to-centre distance-to-diameter (Dctc/Dlat). After evaluating geometric scaling, a representative sub-cohort spanning the volume spectrum was selected to generate 33 high-dose VMAT plans (20 Gy in 2 fractions, D0.03cc ≥ 140%). Dosimetric evaluation was conducted using global indices (PVDR1, PVDR2) and an automated 1D local gradient scoring algorithm (PVDR3, Mean ± SD). MAIN RESULTS: While Dlat and Dctc/Dlat governed geometric scaling, lattice volume occupancy (LVO) and vertex count (Nlat) did not differ significantly across placement models and rotational angles (p > 0.05), indicating that geometric placement results were insensitive to placement strategies. In parameter sensitivity plans, local PVDR3 increased from 1.67 ± 0.28 to 5.41 ± 2.91 as Dctc/Dlat expanded from 2.0 to 3.5. A volume-stratified Dctc/Dlat ratio of 3.0-3.5 was optimal for ensuring geometric eligibility (1% ≤ LVO ≤ 10%) while guaranteeing steep physical gradients (PVDR3 ≥ 3.0): a ratio of 3.5 maximises local fall-off (PVDR3 = 5.41 ± 2.91) in ultra-bulky targets (>1200 cm³), whereas 3.0 is the necessary standard for medium-bulky targets (600-1200 cm³, PVDR3 = 3.05 ± 0.63). Although vertical staggering (Δz) physically reduced local dose bridging (p < 0.01), plan-level PVDR3 showed no statistically significant differences across placement models (p > 0.05). SIGNIFICANCE: This work transitions LRT from empirical trial-and-error to a deterministic, parameter-driven framework. The proposed volume-stratified guidelines, flexible close-packing models, and automated PVDR3 scoring pipeline provide essential physical benchmarks for clinical trial standardisation.

articles.title: Active learning for efficient annotation of surgical videos with weak supervision.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Precise spatial-temporal annotation of laparoscopic videos is time-consuming and requires expert knowledge. We propose a human-in-the-loop knowledge acquisition framework that combines active learning with dual-loss optimization to significantly reduce the annotation effort needed for automatic localization and segmentation of objects in the surgical field. METHODS: Our method employs a foundation model to generate temporally consistent class activation maps (CAMs) from video using two complementary training objectives: a weak supervision loss on video-level tool presence labels for weakly annotated data, and an image-level mask loss on human-corrected annotations obtained through active learning. Rather than requiring dense pixel-level annotation upfront, our pipeline iteratively proposes pseudo-masks that guide the expert annotator to refine the knowledge previously captured by the model. RESULTS: We demonstrate that our framework reduces the effort of surgical video annotation by approximately 50% by the end of training in comparison to fully manual annotation. CONCLUSION: Through eliminating the need for large, fully annotated datasets from the start, this framework enables scalability to the development of surgical tool segmentation models. This iterative human-in-the-loop refinement supports efficient knowledge acquisition with minimal expert input, providing a practical and deployable strategy for expanding tool segmentation to larger, more diverse datasets and real-world clinical settings. Code shared at: https://github.com/PCASOlab/AL-WSL .
articles.journal: Int J Comput Assist Radiol Surg

articles.title: Critical Validation of Deep Learning-Based Cervical Vertebral Fracture Detection on Computed Tomography Localizer Radiographs.
articles.abstract: Localizer radiographs are low-resolution two-dimensional overview images acquired prior to computed tomography (CT) scans. Their automated analysis could support the early detection of cervical vertebral fractures in trauma patients and thus enable immediate adjustment of imaging protocols. This study investigated to what extent deep learning-based methods can reliably detect such fractures on localizer radiographs, with a focus on critically validating model behavior beyond standard performance metrics. On a custom-annotated dataset of 346 trauma patients, two approaches were compared: a full-image binary classification and a two-step pipeline that first localizes the cervical spine and then classifies the cropped region. Model validity was assessed through a permutation test, occlusion testing, gradient-weighted class activation mapping, an analysis of potential confounders, and a subgroup analysis by anatomical fracture location. The full-image classifier formally achieved the highest test-set performance with a precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) of 0.477, compared with 0.349 for the cervical-spine-level classifier. Our validity analysis indicates that the full-image classifier does not primarily rely on the fracture region itself, rendering it unsuitable for clinical use. This work therefore presents a case study of shortcut learning and illustrates validation methods that may be of value for comparable studies on small datasets with visually subtle targets.

articles.title: Multi-task Model with​ Peritumoral MRI Radiomics Learning for Breast Cancer Segmentation-Guided Subtype Classification.
articles.abstract: Accurate breast cancer molecular subtype classification is important for treatment planning, but immunohistochemical assessment may be affected by intratumoral heterogeneity and requires invasive tissue sampling. We hypothesize that segmentation-guided learning of tumor-core and peritumoral microenvironment (PTM) MRI features would improve molecular subtype discrimination over tumor-core-only analysis. A transformer-based segmentation network integrates cross-modal and multi-scale features to delineate tumors, after which the predicted masks are used to construct tumor-core and peritumoral inputs for an energy-regularized classification network. On the test cohort, the retrospective single-center study includes 381 patients with histopathologically confirmed breast cancer and corresponding DCE, DWI, T1WI, and T2WI images. The proposed method achieves a Dice coefficient of 88.29%, a Jaccard index of 79.80%, a precision of 91.98%, and a 95HD of 4.03 pixels for tumor segmentation. For molecular subtype classification, it achieves an accuracy of 84.0%, a macro-averaged sensitivity of 85.7%, a macro-averaged specificity of 94.8%, and a macro-averaged F1 score of 83.9%, providing the best overall performance among the evaluated methods.
